t:
Section 11 of the Water Bank Act (16 U.S.C. 1310) is amended by—

    (1) 
inserting after “program,” in the second sentence the following: “in each fiscal year through the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980,”; and
 
    (2) 
adding at the end thereof two new sentences as follows: “In carrying out the program, in each fiscal year after the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980, the Secretary shall not enter into agreements with owners and operators which would require payments to owners or operators in any calendar year under such agreements in excess of $30,000,000. Not more than 15 percent of the funds authorized to be appropriated in any fiscal year after the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980, may be used for agreements entered into with owners or operators in any one State.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "agreements with owners and operators" brings outside parties into a federal decision. These are conservation payment contracts, comparable to benefit or contract arrangements, and the section only caps annual payments and per-State funding shares. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving non-federal parties.
fable.s: the Secretary shall not enter into agreements with owners and operators which would require payments to owners or operators in any calendar year under such agreements in excess of $30,000,000

qwen_block.w: This section establishes funding caps and limits on agreements between the Secretary and private landowners. Entering into an agreement for payments is a transactional or contractual process, not a participatory decision-making process involving consultation or public input. The text does not require the Secretary to consult with outsiders, hold hearings, or seek comments before making these decisions; it merely restricts the financial scope of the agreements.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary shall not enter into agreements with owners and operators which would require payments to owners or operators in any calendar year under such agreements in excess of $30,000,000.

opus.w: The section limits funding for Water Bank program agreements: it extends the program's timeframe, caps yearly payments and limits how much money can go to any one State. The 'agreements with owners and operators' are payment contracts under a benefits program, which the definition excludes. They are not consultation with outsiders about a federal decision. Nothing here creates a hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: the Secretary shall not enter into agreements with owners and operators which would require payments to owners or operators in any calendar year under such agreements in excess of $30,000,000.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "agreements with owners and operators" means outside parties take part in a federal decision. That fails because these agreements are Water Bank program payment contracts, which are benefit or contract arrangements. The amendment only sets a time limit, a yearly payment cap and a per-State funding limit. It creates no consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes financial and geographic limits on agreements the Secretary enters into with landowners. It does not require the Secretary to consult with these owners, states, or the public before making decisions. Entering into contracts or agreements is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation, which focuses on consultation, coordination, or advisory roles in decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: In carrying out the program, in each fiscal year after the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980, the Secretary shall not enter into agreements with owners and operators which would require payments to owners or operators in any calendar year under such agreements in excess of $30,000,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "entering into agreements with owners and operators" constitutes participation because it involves interaction with outside parties. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" are not participation. Entering into a contract or agreement for land conservation is a transactional/administrative act, not a consultative process where outsiders help shape a federal decision. The section sets financial caps and geographic limits on these agreements but does not require the Secretary to consult with the owners, operators, states, or the public before making the decision to enter into them.
